# <span id="frontmatter2.xhtml_page_vi"></span><span id="frontmatter2.xhtml_kobo.1.1" class="koboSpan">About the Editor</span>

<span id="frontmatter2.xhtml_kobo.2.1" class="koboSpan">Costas Th.
</span><span id="frontmatter2.xhtml_kobo.2.2"
class="koboSpan">Grammenos, CBE, BA (Athens), MSc (Bangor), DSc (City),
FCIB, Hon FIMarEST, FRSA is Professor of Shipping, Trade and Finance;
Pro Vice-Chancellor of City University London and Deputy Dean of its
Cass Business School, where he founded the Centre for Shipping, Trade
and Finance in 1983 (renamed The Costas Grammenos International Centre
for Shipping, Trade and Finance in April 2007).
</span><span id="frontmatter2.xhtml_kobo.2.3" class="koboSpan">The
Centre carries out research through members of its staff and PhD
students and cultivates international dialogue by formal and informal
meetings. </span><span id="frontmatter2.xhtml_kobo.2.4"
class="koboSpan">He designed two world-class Masters of Science:
Shipping, Trade and Finance introduced in 1984; and Logistics, Trade and
Finance commenced in 1997 (since 2008 known as MSc Supply Chain, Trade &
Finance); while the MSc in Energy, Trade and Finance was introduced in
2003.</span>

<span id="frontmatter2.xhtml_kobo.3.1" class="koboSpan">In 1977 he
established credit analysis and policy in bank shipping finance which
has been applied by many international banks; and, in 1978, published
his monograph
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter2.xhtml_kobo.4.1"
class="koboSpan">Bank Finance for Ship
Purchase</span></span><span id="frontmatter2.xhtml_kobo.5.1"
class="koboSpan"> (University of Wales Press), which formed the key
principles in shipping finance.
</span><span id="frontmatter2.xhtml_kobo.5.2" class="koboSpan">In
addition, since mid-1980s, he concentrated on and promoted the
utilisation of international capital markets for raising funds for
shipping companies through his lectures, teaching at University,
conferences and since early 1990s through his published research.
</span><span id="frontmatter2.xhtml_kobo.5.3" class="koboSpan">In 2006
he was appointed by the Greek government as President of the Managing
Board of the International Hellenic University in Thessaloniki, Greece,
with the mandate to establish and operate it.
</span><span id="frontmatter2.xhtml_kobo.5.4" class="koboSpan">His
research interests are in Bank Shipping Finance, and Capital
Markets.</span>

<span id="frontmatter2.xhtml_kobo.6.1" class="koboSpan">In 1999 Costas
Grammenos was awarded by City University London the highest academic
accolade, the Doctor of Science degree (DSc) for creating, through his
published research, shipping finance as a new academic
discipline.</span>

<span id="frontmatter2.xhtml_kobo.7.1" class="koboSpan">He is a member
of the Board of Directors of the Alexander S Onassis Public Benefit
Foundation; a Founding Trustee of the Institute of Marine Engineers
Memorial Fund; and a Non-executive member of the Board, Marfin
Investment Group (MIG).</span>

<span id="frontmatter2.xhtml_kobo.8.1" class="koboSpan">He is Fellow of
the Chartered Institute of Bankers; Honorary Fellow, Institute of Marine
Engineers, Science and Technology; Fellow of Royal Society of Arts and
Member of the Baltic Exchange; Member of the American Bureau of
Shipping; Liveryman of the Worshipful Company of Shipwrights; Freeman of
the City of London; Founder and Chairman of the City of London Biennial
Meetings; Visiting Professor at the University of Antwerp; and he was
President of IAME (1997–2002).</span>

<span id="frontmatter2.xhtml_kobo.9.1" class="koboSpan">He was 1998
Seatrade Personality of the Year; in 2008 he was awarded the prize of
Distinguished Personality for his outstanding contribution to the
shipping industry by the Association of Banking and Financial Executives
of Hellenic Shipping; and in 2009 was awarded the ‘Achievement in
Education’ at the Lloyd’s List Shipping Awards; he was made OBE (Officer
of the British Empire) in 1994 for his contribution to international
shipping and finance and appointed CBE (Commander of the British Empire)
in 2008 for services to teaching and research.</span>

</div>

</div>

<span id="Preface1.xhtml"></span>

<div id="Preface1.xhtml_book-columns">

<div id="Preface1.xhtml_book-inner">

# <span id="Preface1.xhtml_page_vii"></span>[<span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.1.1" class="koboSpan">Preface to the Second Edition </span>](#contents.xhtml_bck_ht0003)

<span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.2.1" class="koboSpan">In the seven years
that have passed since 2002, when the first edition of this
</span><span class="italic"><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.3.1"
class="koboSpan">Handbook
</span></span><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.4.1" class="koboSpan">was
published, each one of us would have noticed major events or conditions
that have strongly impacted the shipping markets and produced results
that we would include in our lectures – often we categorise these as
extraordinary.</span>

<span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.5.1" class="koboSpan">I have in mind the
explosive rate of growth in China; the almost unstoppable increase in
seaborne trade and in investments in new vessels; in the expansion in
number and size of Chinese shipyards; in the continuation of bank
finance as the strong source of funds for shipping companies; in the
mergers or acquisitions of shipping companies and, generally, in the
increase of their size; and in the emergence of capital markets as a
serious means of raising funds for a sizeable number of shipping
companies.</span>

<span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.6.1" class="koboSpan">All this activity
was abruptly shaken in 2007 when the world recession shyly emerged and
the subprime crisis of US residential mortgages, and the toxic products
based on them, hit the international financial system and froze the
liquidity in it.</span>

<span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.7.1" class="koboSpan">It seems we have not
seen the end of the mega drama that we have witnessed in these seven
years.</span>

<span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.8.1" class="koboSpan">Our
</span><span class="italic"><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.9.1"
class="koboSpan">Handbook</span></span><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.10.1"
class="koboSpan"> has been directly or indirectly influenced by events
of the first decade of the 21st century which have been embodied in our
data analysis. </span><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.10.2"
class="koboSpan">The structure of this volume remains the same as the
edition published in 2002. </span><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.10.3"
class="koboSpan">However, in addition to the rewriting or updating of
the chapters, some new topics have been included in the volume, such as
the historical analysis of freight rates fluctuations in
</span><a href="#Ch010.xhtml_ht0244" id="Preface1.xhtml_bck_ht0244"><span
id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.11.1" class="koboSpan">chapter 10</span></a><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.12.1"
class="koboSpan">; measures for global control of air pollution from
ships in
</span><a href="#Ch016.xhtml_ht0373" id="Preface1.xhtml_bck_ht0373"><span
id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.13.1" class="koboSpan">chapter 16</span></a><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.14.1"
class="koboSpan">; measures for business performance in shipping in
</span><a href="#Ch022.xhtml_ht0474" id="Preface1.xhtml_bck_ht0474"><span
id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.15.1" class="koboSpan">chapter 22</span></a><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.16.1"
class="koboSpan">; while capital markets as a source in shipping finance
and a holistic survey in strategy literature relevant to shipping are
discussed in
</span><a href="#Ch028.xhtml_ht0619" id="Preface1.xhtml_bck_ht0619"><span
id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.17.1" class="koboSpan"> chapters 28</span></a><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.18.1"
class="koboSpan"> and
</span><a href="#Ch029.xhtml_ht0648" id="Preface1.xhtml_bck_ht0648"><span
id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.19.1" class="koboSpan">29</span></a><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.20.1"
class="koboSpan"> respectively.</span>

<span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.21.1" class="koboSpan">The first edition
established the
</span><span class="italic"><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.22.1"
class="koboSpan">Handbook</span></span><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.23.1"
class="koboSpan"> as an authoritative source of academic research that
is useful for university students and researchers and, at the same time,
it satisfies the curiosity of the well-informed practitioner and widens
its knowledge horizon. </span><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.23.2"
class="koboSpan">It is a pleasure to know that the
</span><span class="italic"><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.24.1"
class="koboSpan">Handbook</span></span><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.25.1"
class="koboSpan"> is now called “The Maritime Bible” in more than 30
countries.</span>

<span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.26.1" class="koboSpan">I want to thank all
my colleagues for their enthusiasm to participate in the 2002 and 2010
editions and to thank them profoundly for the high quality of their
contributions.</span>

<span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.27.1" class="koboSpan">Finally, I want to
thank my Personal Assistant, Chrysoula Zevgolatakou, for controlling the
logistics of incoming and outgoing chapters and the Informa editorial
and printing staff, in particular Liz Lewis and Leigh Stutter, for their
cooperation and patience in meeting tight deadlines.</span>

<span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.28.1" class="koboSpan">Needless to report
that as contributors we again gave up our royalties in favour of the
International Association of Maritime Economies (IAME) and continue to
be loyal members.</span>

<span class="italic"><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.29.1"
class="koboSpan">Professor Costas Th.
</span><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.29.2"
class="koboSpan">Grammenos</span></span>\
<span class="italic"><span id="Preface1.xhtml_kobo.30.1"
class="koboSpan">London, June 2010</span></span>

</div>

</div>

<span id="Preface2.xhtml"></span>

<div id="Preface2.xhtml_book-columns">

<div id="Preface2.xhtml_book-inner">

# <span id="Preface2.xhtml_page_viii"></span><span id="Preface2.xhtml_page_ix"></span>[<span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.1.1" class="koboSpan">Preface to the First Edition </span>](#contents.xhtml_bck_ht0004)

<span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.2.1" class="koboSpan">In the late 1960s,
when I started focusing on shipping finance, there were only a limited
number of publications on Maritime Economics which mainly analysed the
broader theoretical topics. </span><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.2.2"
class="koboSpan">Now, after almost thirty-five years, this unique volume
is published, covering for the first time a wide variety of maritime
issues and sectors, written by fifty-one members of the International
Association of Maritime Economists (IAME).
</span><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.2.3" class="koboSpan">Over forty of
the contributors are well-known academics, with the remaining younger
ones already showing recognisable academic presence, all teaching and
conducting research at thirty universities, in seventeen
countries.</span>

<span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.3.1" class="koboSpan">IAME was established
in 1992 with an aim to promote the development of maritime economics as
a distinct discipline, to encourage rational and reasoned discussion
within it, and to facilitate the international exchange of ideas and
research. </span><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.3.2"
class="koboSpan">Throughout this decade, IAME has worked towards these
aims most successfully, and here one should mention the organisation of
international conferences, on an annual basis; this year (on its tenth
anniversary), members will meet in Panama.</span>

<span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.4.1" class="koboSpan">The
</span><span class="italic"><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.5.1"
class="koboSpan">Handbook of Maritime Economics and
Business</span></span><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.6.1"
class="koboSpan"> contains thirty-nine refereed chapters which are,
primarily, based on research carried out over a number of years,
covering eleven broad areas of Maritime Economics,
</span><span class="italic"><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.7.1"
class="koboSpan">viz</span></span><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.8.1"
class="koboSpan">: Maritime Economics and Globalisation; International
Seaborne Trade; Economics of Shipping Markets and Cycles; Economics of
Shipping Sectors; Issues in Liner Shipping; Maritime Safety and Labour
Markets; National and International Shipping Policies; Aspects of
Shipping Management and Operations; Shipping Investment and Finance;
Port Economics and Management; and Aspects of International
Logistics.</span>

<span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.9.1" class="koboSpan">As I was studying
these chapters, not only did I recall the questions that arose when I
was collecting data for my study in Bank Shipping Finance, all those
years ago, when so many answers were not readily available in published
paper form or any other publication, I also found myself smiling many
times, with great satisfaction, as I measured the width and depth of
research presented here, in the wider spectrum of Maritime Economics.
</span><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.9.2" class="koboSpan">Indeed,
</span><span class="italic"><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.10.1"
class="koboSpan">The Handbook of Maritime Economics and
Business</span></span><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.11.1"
class="koboSpan"> is unique as it demonstrates the immeasurable
progress, since the 1960s, in this area of research and teaching.</span>

<span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.12.1" class="koboSpan">Because of its high
quality output and its relevance to real life business, it will serve as
a very valuable instrument for the stakeholders of the broader maritime
world, including: university undergraduate and postgraduate students;
shipowners; shipbrokers; shipmanagers and operators; bankers;
underwriters; lawyers; shipping consultants; international logistics
companies; port authorities; governmental maritime agencies; and
official international organisations.</span>

<span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.13.1" class="koboSpan">Over the last six
months, I have worked closely with all the contributors and I thank them
</span><span class="italic"><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.14.1"
class="koboSpan">de
profundis</span></span><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.15.1"
class="koboSpan"> for the spontaneous acceptance of my invitation and
the prompt delivery of what they promised.
</span><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.15.2" class="koboSpan">I am also
grateful to them for agreeing, like myself, to waive their royalties in
favour of IAME. </span><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.15.3"
class="koboSpan">My sincere thanks go to David Gilbertson,
</span><span id="Preface2.xhtml_page_x"></span><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.16.1"
class="koboSpan">Chief Executive of Informa Group, who from the early
days has strongly supported the idea of this volume; also to the LLP
editorial and printing staff, in particular Vanessa Larkin and Tony
Lansbury, for their cooperation and patience in meeting the tight
deadlines. </span><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.16.2"
class="koboSpan">Finally, I thank very warmly two members of my staff:
Dr Amir Alizadeh, also a contributor to this volume, and my Personal
Assistant, Mrs Gladys Parish, for their enthusiasm and valuable
assistance in the preparation of this
</span><span class="italic"><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.17.1"
class="koboSpan">Handbook</span></span><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.18.1"
class="koboSpan">.</span>

<span class="italic"><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.19.1"
class="koboSpan">Professor Costas
Th</span></span><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.20.1"
class="koboSpan">.</span><span class="italic"><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.21.1"
class="koboSpan"> Grammenos</span></span>\
<span class="italic"><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.22.1"
class="koboSpan">London</span></span><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.23.1"
class="koboSpan">,</span><span class="italic"><span id="Preface2.xhtml_kobo.24.1"
class="koboSpan"> September 2002</span></span>

</div>

</div>

# <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_page_xiv"></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_page_xv"></span>[<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.1.1" class="koboSpan">List of Contributors </span>](#contents.xhtml_bck_ht0006)

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.2.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Patrick M. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.2.2" class="koboSpan">Alderton</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.3.1" class="koboSpan">Born in 1931 and
educated for the usual period, though left the sixth form to run away to
sea in 1948 in BTC (later known as BP Tankers).
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.3.2" class="koboSpan">Later in
1959, after trying most types of ships, he obtained his Extra Masters
Certificate and lectured in one of the two navigation schools in London
that in the late 1960s were amalgamated into the City of London
Polytechnic. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.3.3"
class="koboSpan">In the 1970s he moved to the Transport Department of
the CLP and worked on his MPhil which he obtained in 1973.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.3.4" class="koboSpan">In 1989
he joined the World Maritime University as Professor of Ports and
Shipping where he remained until he retired in 1995.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.3.5" class="koboSpan">Since
then he has been a visiting professor at the London Metropolitan
University. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.3.6"
class="koboSpan">Publications include
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.4.1"
class="koboSpan">Sea Transport – Operations & Economics
</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.5.1"
class="koboSpan">(6th edn) and
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.6.1"
class="koboSpan">Port Management and Operations
</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.7.1"
class="koboSpan">(3rd edn), plus over 100 papers, articles and chapters
in various books.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.8.1" class="koboSpan">Dr Amir H. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.8.2" class="koboSpan">Alizadeh</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.9.1" class="koboSpan">Amir Alizadeh is
a Reader in “Shipping Economics and Finance” at Cass Business School,
City University London, and a visiting professor at Copenhagen Business
School and University of Geneva.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.9.2" class="koboSpan">He has
first degree in Nautical Studies from Iran and worked as a ship officer
for a short time. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.9.3"
class="koboSpan">He then joined Cass Business School where he finished
his MSc in Shipping, Trade and Finance and a PhD in Finance.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.9.4" class="koboSpan">He
teaches different topics including Quantitative Methods, Oil & Energy
Transportation and Logistics, Shipping Investment and Finance,
Econometric Modelling, Energy and Weather Derivatives, and Shipping Risk
Management. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.9.5"
class="koboSpan">His research interest includes, modelling freight
markets and markets for ships, derivatives and risk management in
financial and commodity markets, and econometrics and forecasting.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.9.6" class="koboSpan">He has
published in several academic journals in the area of transportation,
finance and economics. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.9.7"
class="koboSpan">Apart from academic research, he has been in close
contact with the industry both as an advisor and as a consultant.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.9.8" class="koboSpan">He is
involved in running the Baltic Exchange courses in “Freight Derivatives
& Shipping Risk Management” and “Advanced Freight Modelling and Trading”
which are offered in maritime centres worldwide.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.10.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Alfred J. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.10.2" class="koboSpan">Baird</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.11.1" class="koboSpan">Alfred J.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.11.2" class="koboSpan">Baird is
Professor of Maritime Transport at the Transport Research Institute
(TRI), Edinburgh Napier University.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.11.3" class="koboSpan">His
doctoral research concerned the study of strategic management in the
global container shipping industry.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.11.4" class="koboSpan">He has a
BA (Hons) in Business Studies and is a Member of the Chartered Institute
of Logistics & Transport. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.11.5"
class="koboSpan">Prior to his academic career he worked for a liner
shipping company. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.11.6"
class="koboSpan">With an emphasis on the ferry and container shipping
sectors, and the ports industry in general, Professor Baird has
researched, published, advised, and taught across a range of maritime
transport subjects including: strategic management in shipping, shipping
market and industry analysis, ship and port cost modelling, shipping
service scheduling/planning, competition, privatisation, procurement and
tendering of shipping services, government policy, state subsidies, and
assessing the feasibility of shipping services and port
facilities.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_page_xvi"></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.12.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Helen Bendall</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.13.1" class="koboSpan">Helen Bendall
is a Director of MariTrade, a consultancy firm specialising in maritime
investment and trade statistics for the maritime and aviation
industries. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.13.2"
class="koboSpan">Dr Bendall is a popular guest speaker on shipping
investment and technological change in industry conferences and is an
advisor to several peak industry and policy councils, having taken an
active role in IMO working parties.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.13.3"
class="koboSpan">Currently teaching at the Macquarie University in
Sydney, she was also a senior academic member of UTS where she
specialised in International Financial Management in the Finance and
Economics School. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.13.4"
class="koboSpan">She is well known for cross–disciplinary financial
analysis to shipping and maritime investment problems.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.13.5" class="koboSpan">Her PhD
on the economics of technological change in shipping included an
innovative approach to measuring ship and cargo handling productivity
across several ship types.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.13.6" class="koboSpan">Many of
her subsequent publications have analysed applications of new shipping
technology such as advanced algorithms to solve complex fast ship
scheduling problems. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.13.7"
class="koboSpan">More recently her research focused on the application
of real options analysis to evaluate the financial viability of new ship
technology and complex ship investment decisions.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.14.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Mary R. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.14.2" class="koboSpan">Brooks</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.15.1" class="koboSpan">Mary R.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.15.2" class="koboSpan">Brooks
is the William A. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.15.3"
class="koboSpan">Black Chair of Commerce at Dalhousie University,
Halifax, Canada. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.15.4"
class="koboSpan">From February 2002 to April 2008, she chaired the
Committee on International Trade and Transportation, until recently
served on the Committee for Funding Options for Freight Transportation
Projects of National Significance, and currently serves on the
Publication Board of the
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.16.1"
class="koboSpan">Transportation Research
Record</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.17.1"
class="koboSpan">, of the Transportation Research Board, Washington DC.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.17.2" class="koboSpan">She was
appointed to the Marine Board of the US National Academy of Sciences for
three years in November 2008.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.17.3" class="koboSpan">She
chairs the Port Performance Research Network, a network of scholars
interested in port governance and port performance issues.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.17.4" class="koboSpan">She was
a Canada–US Fulbright scholar at George Mason University in 2005.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.17.5" class="koboSpan">Her
latest book,
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.18.1"
class="koboSpan">North American Freight Transportation: The Road to
Security and
Prosperity</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.19.1"
class="koboSpan">, was published in June 2008.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.19.2" class="koboSpan">In
November 2006, she was named by the Women’s Executive Network as
Canada’s Most Powerful Women: Top 100 in the professional
category.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.20.1" class="koboSpan">Dr Ana Cristina Paixão Casaca</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.21.1" class="koboSpan">Ana Cristina
Paixão Casaca is the Technical director of ESPRIM – Centro de
Acostagens, Amarrações e Serviços Marítimos, Lda.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.21.2" class="koboSpan">She
obtained her elementary nautical studies degree at Escola Náutica
Infante D. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.21.3"
class="koboSpan">Henrique (ENIDH) in Paço D’Arcos, Portugal.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.21.4" class="koboSpan">She was
a deck officer in Portuguese shipping companies and lectured at the
Instituto de Tecnologias Náuticas.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.21.5" class="koboSpan">She
received her BA in 1995, and subsequently obtained an MSc in
International Logistics at the Institute of Marine Studies, University
of Plymouth in 1997. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.21.6"
class="koboSpan">She completed her PhD in International
Transport/Logistics at the University of Wales, Cardiff in 2003.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.21.7" class="koboSpan">Since
1998, she has published articles in professional magazines and
well-known international academic journals.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.21.8" class="koboSpan">She is a
member of the Institute of Chartered Shipbrokers (ICS) and of the
International Association of Maritime Economists (IAME).
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.21.9" class="koboSpan">Since
2003, she has evaluated transport related projects and proposals on
behalf of the European Commission.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.21.10" class="koboSpan">She is
a guest lecturer at the Netherlands Maritime University.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_page_xvii"></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.22.1" class="koboSpan">Professor A. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.22.2" class="koboSpan">Güldem Cerit</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.23.1" class="koboSpan">Güldem Cerit
received her BSc degree from the Engineering School of the Middle East
Technical University, Ankara, Turkey.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.23.2" class="koboSpan">She
worked in private industry for nine years and in 1993, joined the Dokuz
Eylul University School of Maritime Business and Management (which
became the Maritime Faculty in 2009) as an Assistant Professor.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.23.3" class="koboSpan">Dr Cerit
has served as the Director/Dean of the Faculty since 1997.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.24.1" class="koboSpan">Dr Cimen Karatas Cetin</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.25.1" class="koboSpan">Cimen Karatas
Cetin has lectured on maritime business, port management and operations
at the Dokuz Eylul University, Maritime Faculty in Izmir, Turkey since
2003. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.25.2"
class="koboSpan">She completed her MSc at the Dokuz Eylul University
Institute of Social Sciences in Maritime Business Administration in
2004, and pursues her doctoral studies in the same department.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.25.3" class="koboSpan">She was
awarded a grant by the Scientific and Technological Research Council of
Turkey (TUBITAK) in 2008 and continued her doctoral research at the
Erasmus University Rotterdam, Center for Maritime Economics and
Logistics (MEL) as a research fellow in 2009/2010.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.25.4" class="koboSpan">She has
presented several papers on port management and organisation at
international conferences, has published articles in journals and in
edited books. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.25.5"
class="koboSpan">She has participated in transport and port-related
projects in Turkey.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.26.1" class="koboSpan">Steve Christy</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.27.1" class="koboSpan">Steve Christy
is Head of Consultancy & Research at Gibson Shipbrokers, based in
London. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.27.2"
class="koboSpan">He has more than 25 years’ experience in the tanker and
oil industries, covering oil supply and transportation developments.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.27.3" class="koboSpan">He is
now responsible for Gibson’s analysis of all the shipping markets.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.27.4" class="koboSpan">This
includes research into market and industry developments impacting on the
tanker industry, the implications for future supply and demand of
tankers and forecast analysis of charter rates and earnings.</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.28.1" class="koboSpan">He has worked
on a number of major projects, including various tanker market forecasts
for different shipowners, charterers and investment clients.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.28.2" class="koboSpan">He is
also involved in cost analysis, transportation options and shipping
economics, and tanker investment appraisal, as well as acting as an
expert witness in legal cases.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.29.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Kevin Cullinane</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.30.1" class="koboSpan">Kevin Cullinane
is Director of the Transport Research Institute and Professor of
International Logistics at Edinburgh Napier University.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.30.2" class="koboSpan">He was
formerly Chair in Marine Transport & Management at Newcastle University,
Professor and Head of the Department of Shipping & Transport Logistics
at the Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Head of the Centre for
International Shipping & Transport at Plymouth University, Senior
Partner in his own transport consultancy company and Research Fellow at
the University of Oxford Transport Studies Unit.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.30.3" class="koboSpan">He is a
Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Logistics & Transport, and has been
a logistics adviser to the World Bank and transport adviser to the
governments of Scotland, Ireland, Hong Kong, Egypt, Chile, Korea and the
UK. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.30.4" class="koboSpan">He
is a Visiting Professor at the University of Gothenburg, holds an
Honorary Professorship at the University of Hong Kong and has published
seven books and over 180 refereed journal and conference papers.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.30.5" class="koboSpan">He also
sits on the editorial boards of several journals.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_page_xviii"></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.31.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Douglas K. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.31.2" class="koboSpan">Fleming</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.32.1" class="koboSpan">Douglas Fleming
is a maritime geographer and professor emeritus at the University of
Washington, Seattle. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.32.2"
class="koboSpan">He earned an undergraduate degree in Geology at
Princeton in 1943 and a PhD in Geography at Seattle in 1965.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.32.3" class="koboSpan">He
served with the US Navy from 1944 to 1946.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.32.4" class="koboSpan">He was
employed by a commercial steamship line for 15 years in various
capacities including chartering brokerage and as vice president of
States Marine and Isthmian traffic operations in New York, Houston and
Seattle. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.32.5"
class="koboSpan">From 1965 to 2002 he taught various classes in
Geography and Marine Affairs at the University of Washington, Seattle.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.32.6" class="koboSpan">He has
contributed numerous articles to American and European journals and has
served periodically on editorial boards in Europe.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.33.1" class="koboSpan">Dr David Glen</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.34.1" class="koboSpan">David Glen is
Reader in Transport in the Business School, London Metropolitan
University, having joined the Centre for International Transport
Management in 1995, as a Research Fellow.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.34.2" class="koboSpan">He
obtained his PhD from London Business School in 1987, which examined
differentiation in the tanker market.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.34.3" class="koboSpan">He has
published in a number of journals, including the
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.35.1"
class="koboSpan">Journal of Transport Economics and
Policy</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.36.1"
class="koboSpan"> and
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.37.1"
class="koboSpan">Maritime Policy and
Management</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.38.1"
class="koboSpan">. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.38.2"
class="koboSpan">He is presently on the editorial board of the latter.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.38.3" class="koboSpan">Dr Glen
served on the Council of IAME for a number of years, and was Secretary
from 2000 to 2003. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.38.4"
class="koboSpan">He is also a member of the International Maritime
Statistics Forum. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.38.5"
class="koboSpan">His research interests include shipping market
structures and dynamics, seafarer statistics, maritime pollution and
international trade flows.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.38.6" class="koboSpan">Since
1997, he has been involved UK Department for Transport projects on
monitoring and improving the quality of UK seafarer numbers.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.39.1" class="koboSpan">Dr Stephen X. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.39.2" class="koboSpan">H. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.39.3" class="koboSpan">Gong</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.40.1" class="koboSpan">Stephen X.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.40.2" class="koboSpan">H.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.40.3" class="koboSpan">Gong is
with the School of Accounting and Finance at the Hong Kong Polytechnic
University. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.40.4"
class="koboSpan">He was initially trained in Shipping, Trade and Finance
at Cass Business School, City University London and subsequently
completed a PhD in Finance at the Hong Kong Polytechnic University.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.40.5" class="koboSpan">His
research interests span the areas of corporate finance, corporate
governance, financial reporting, industrial organisation, and
transportation economics. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.40.6"
class="koboSpan">He has consulted with international as well as local
organisations in the areas of logistics development and transportation
investment and finance.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.41.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Gelina Harlaftis</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.42.1" class="koboSpan">Gelina
Harlaftis graduated from the University of Athens and completed her
graduate studies in the Universities of Cambridge (MPhil) and Oxford
(DPhil), in St Antony’s College between 1983 and 1988.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.42.2" class="koboSpan">She
taught at the University of Piraeus from 1991 to 2002 and since 2003 has
been at the Department of History of the Ionian University.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.42.3" class="koboSpan">She was
President of the International Association of Maritime Economic History
from 2004 to 2008. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.42.4"
class="koboSpan">During the fall of the academic year 2008–2009 she was
Alfred D. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.42.5"
class="koboSpan">Chandler Jr.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.42.6"
class="koboSpan">International Visiting Scholar in the Business History
Program of the Harvard Business School and in the spring a Visiting
Fellow at All Souls College, Oxford.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.42.7" class="koboSpan">She is
the author of several books including
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.43.1"
class="koboSpan">Greek Shipowners and Greece 1945–1975
</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.44.1"
class="koboSpan">(Athlone Press, 1993), and her latest book,
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.45.1"
class="koboSpan">Leadership in World Shipping: Greek Family Firms in
International Business
</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.46.1"
class="koboSpan">with Ioannis Theotokas, was published in 2009.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_page_xix"></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.47.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Trevor D. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.47.2" class="koboSpan">Heaver</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.48.1" class="koboSpan">Trevor Heaver
is professor emeritus at the University of British Columbia where he was
the UPS Foundation Professor and Director for the Centre for
Transportation Studies. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.48.2"
class="koboSpan">Since retiring from UBC, he has been Visiting Professor
at the University of Antwerp (on-going), the University of Sydney
(Australia) and the University of Stellenbosch.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.48.3" class="koboSpan">He is a
founding member and a Past-President of the International Association of
Maritime Economists and a Past-Chairman of the World Conference on
Transport Research. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.48.4"
class="koboSpan">He has published widely on transportation, logistics
and transportation policy and has served as a consultant to corporations
and governments in Canada and internationally.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.49.1" class="koboSpan">Dr Jan Hoffman</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.50.1" class="koboSpan">Jan Hoffmann
works as trade facilitation, port and shipping specialist at UNCTAD’s
Trade Logistics Branch since 2003 and is currently chief of the Trade
Facilitation section. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.50.2"
class="koboSpan">He is in charge of a trade facilitation project on WTO
negotiations, as well as national projects in Afghanistan and Pakistan.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.50.3" class="koboSpan">He edits
the UNCTAD
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.51.1"
class="koboSpan">Transport
Newsletter</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.52.1"
class="koboSpan"> and is co-author of the annual
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.53.1"
class="koboSpan">Review of Maritime
Transport</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.54.1"
class="koboSpan">.</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.55.1" class="koboSpan">Previously, he
spent six years with the United Nations Economic Commission for Latin
America and the Caribbean, Santiago de Chile, and two years with the
IMO, London. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.55.2"
class="koboSpan">Prior to this, he held part-time positions as assistant
professor, import-export agent, translator, consultant and seafarer for
a tramp shipping company.</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.56.1" class="koboSpan">Jan has studied
in Germany, the UK and Spain, and holds a doctorate degree in Economics
from the University of Hamburg.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.56.2" class="koboSpan">His work
has resulted in numerous UN and peer-reviewed publications, lectures and
technical missions, as well as the internet
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.57.1"
class="koboSpan">Maritime
Profile</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.58.1"
class="koboSpan">, the
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.59.1"
class="koboSpan">International Transport Data
Base</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.60.1"
class="koboSpan">, the
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.61.1"
class="koboSpan">Liner Shipping Connectivity
Index</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.62.1"
class="koboSpan">, and various electronic newsletters.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.63.1" class="koboSpan">Mr William Homan-Russell</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.64.1" class="koboSpan">William
Homan-Russell received an MSc in Finance from London Business School in
2007 and an MA in Mathematics from Oxford University in 2002.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.64.2" class="koboSpan">He
joined Tufton Oceanic Ltd in 2003 as a financial analyst to work on
credit and market analysis of the shipping sector for the company’s
leasing and corporate advisory departments.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.64.3" class="koboSpan">William
subsequently joined Tufton’s Oceanic Hedge Fund in 2006 to work within
the shipping team; he focuses on the modelling of global publicly listed
shipping equities and shipping market models as well as developing
quantitative portfolio optimisation procedures.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.64.4" class="koboSpan">His MSc
in Finance was completed whilst with Tufton Oceanic Ltd.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.65.1" class="koboSpan">Dr Gordon Hui</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.66.1" class="koboSpan">Gordon Hui
graduated as a MPhil in Physics in 2006.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.66.2" class="koboSpan">He
specialised in computer simulations for condensed matter systems by
matrix & Monte Carlo algorithms.</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.67.1" class="koboSpan">He started his
career in financial industry as a quantitative researcher in a Commodity
Trading Advisor; his areas of expertise being Monte Carlo simulations in
risk management and rebalancing portfolios, volatility modelling in
various time frame, backtesting in Market-On-Close, day-trading
strategies & HK index arbitrage.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.67.2"
class="koboSpan">Afterwards, he worked as a quantitative day-trader in a
propriety trading house. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.67.3"
class="koboSpan">In 2009, Gordon joined Tufton as an analyst.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_page_xx"></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.68.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Joon Soo Jon</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.69.1" class="koboSpan">Joon Soo Jon
began his academic life with a BA in English Literature from Sogang
University, and went on to obtain a Master’s degree in Transport
Management at SUNY and a doctorate in Maritime Studies at the University
of Wales in Cardiff. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.69.2"
class="koboSpan">He is currently a professor at Sogang University in
Seoul. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.69.3"
class="koboSpan">While teaching and researching in the maritime sector,
he has been involved in policy making as an adviser to various Korean
Government agencies such as the Ministry of Maritime Affairs, the
Ministry of Industry and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.69.4" class="koboSpan">He has
published widely. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.69.5"
class="koboSpan">His current research interests focus upon the
development of logistics systems in the Far Eastern Countries.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.70.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Manolis G. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.70.2" class="koboSpan">Kavussanos</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.71.1" class="koboSpan">Manolis
Kavussanos is a faculty member of the Athens University of Economics and
Business (AUEB), Greece. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.71.2"
class="koboSpan">He is the Director of the MSc and PhD programmes in
Accounting and Finance and of the Research Centre for Finance at AUEB.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.71.3" class="koboSpan">He holds
a BSc and MSc (Economics) from London University and a PhD (Applied
Economics) from Cass Business School, City University London.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.71.4" class="koboSpan">He
directed the MSc in Trade, Logistics and Finance at Cass from its
inception until he joined AUEB.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.71.5" class="koboSpan">He has
held various posts as professor of finance and shipping in universities
in more than eight countries around the globe.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.71.6" class="koboSpan">He has
written extensively in the areas of finance, shipping and applied
economics, published in top international refereed journals, in
conference proceedings and books.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.71.7" class="koboSpan">This
work has been presented in international conferences and professional
meetings around the world, gaining awards for its quality, being
sponsored by both public and private sector companies and being cited
extensively by other researchers in the area.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.71.8" class="koboSpan">Since
1992 he has worked in developing the area of risk analysis and
management in shipping and is the author of the book
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.72.1"
class="koboSpan">Derivatives and Risk Management in
Shipping</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.73.1"
class="koboSpan">.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.74.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Shashi Kumar</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.75.1" class="koboSpan">Shashi Kumar is
the Interim Superintendent/Academic Dean at the United States Merchant
Marine Academy in Kings Point, New York.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.75.2" class="koboSpan">He is
also the Founding Dean of the Loeb-Sullivan School of International
Business and Logistics at Maine Maritime Academy in Maine, USA.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.75.3" class="koboSpan">He is a
Master Mariner (UK) and sailed extensively on commercial ships prior to
entering academe. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.75.4"
class="koboSpan">Dr Kumar is a founding member of IAME and the
International Association of Maritime Universities, and is also
affiliated with the American Society of Transportation and Logistics.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.75.5" class="koboSpan">His
areas of teaching and research include maritime economics and policies,
international shipping, and maritime logistics.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.75.6" class="koboSpan">He has
published extensively and authors an annual review of the shipping
industry for the US Naval Institute.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.75.7" class="koboSpan">He has
held visiting professor appointments at the Indian Institute of
Management-Ahmedabad (India), Memorial University (Canada), World
Maritime University (Sweden), Shanghai Maritime University (China) and
the Pontifical Catholic University (Puerto Rico).</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.76.1" class="koboSpan">Dr Neophytos Lambertides</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.77.1" class="koboSpan">Neophytos
Lambertides received a BSc in Mathematics and Statistics from the
University of Cyprus in 2000 and an MSc in Financial Mathematics from
the University of Warwick in 2001.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.77.2" class="koboSpan">He took
a PhD in Finance from the University of Cyprus in 2006.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.77.3"
class="koboSpan">Thereafter,
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_page_xxi"></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.78.1"
class="koboSpan">he was designated as a Visiting Scholar at Columbia
Business School. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.78.2"
class="koboSpan">He is currently lecturer in Finance at Aston Business
School (UK). </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.78.3"
class="koboSpan">His interests are mainly on the area of asset pricing,
credit risk and bankruptcy prediction, option pricing theory, real
options, and shipping finance.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.78.4" class="koboSpan">His
publications appeared in the
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.79.1"
class="koboSpan">Journal of Accounting Auditing and Finance, Abacus, The
British Account Review, Managerial Finance, Maritime Policy &
Management</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.80.1"
class="koboSpan">. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.80.2"
class="koboSpan">He reviewed papers for, among others, the
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.81.1"
class="koboSpan">European Journal of Operational Research and Managerial
Finance</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.82.1"
class="koboSpan">.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.83.1" class="koboSpan">Dr Ana Rita Lynce</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.84.1" class="koboSpan">Ana Rita Lynce
is currently working for Ascendi S.A.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.84.2" class="koboSpan">which is
providing technical support to a road concessionaire in the state of São
Paulo, Brazil called Rodovias do Tietê.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.84.3" class="koboSpan">Subject
to the Bolonha process, Ana Rita obtained her MSc in Civil Engineering
and specialised in Land Planning, Transportation and Management, at the
Technical University of Lisbon – Instituto Superior Técnico, Lisbon,
Portugal. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.84.4"
class="koboSpan">She developed a thesis on the
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.85.1"
class="koboSpan">Barriers and potentialities of rail freight from the
Iberian Peninsula to
Europe</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.86.1"
class="koboSpan"> at the Centre for Innovation in Transport (CENIT) –
Technical University of Catalonia, in Barcelona.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.86.2" class="koboSpan">After
finishing her thesis, she started to work as a Transport Researcher in
the railway department of CENIT.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.86.3" class="koboSpan">In
September 2007, she became a Transport Researcher at the Department of
Economics and Quantitative methods (DIEM) – University of Genoa, in
Genoa and a Guest Scientific Assistant at the Laboratory for
Intermodality and Transport Planning (LITEP) – École Polytechnique
Fédérale de Lausanne in Switzerland, with a TransportNET scholarship,
funded by the EU under the Sixth Framework Marie Curie Actions
Programme. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.86.4"
class="koboSpan">Since 2008, she has presented research papers at
conferences on Transport and Logistics in areas such as the
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.87.1"
class="koboSpan">Extension of the European high-speed railway network
and Transport sustainability strategies for supply chain management in
the fast moving consumer goods
industry</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.88.1"
class="koboSpan">. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.88.2"
class="koboSpan">In 2009, she published a research paper on
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.89.1"
class="koboSpan">Short Sea Shipping and
Intermodality</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.90.1"
class="koboSpan"> in the journal
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.91.1"
class="koboSpan">NETNOMICS</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.92.1"
class="koboSpan">. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.92.2"
class="koboSpan">In the same year, she worked at VTM – Consultores, a
Transport Consultancy Company in Portugal in a project for RAVE, the
Portuguese High-Speed Rail Infrastructure Manager.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.93.1" class="koboSpan">Dr Shuo Ma</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.94.1" class="koboSpan">Shuo Ma is a
professor of shipping and port economics and policy at the World
Maritime University in Malmö.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.94.2" class="koboSpan">He is
also Vice-President (Academic) at WMU.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.94.3" class="koboSpan">Dr Ma is
an active researcher and consultant in the area of shipping and port
economics and policy. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.94.4"
class="koboSpan">For the last couple of years, he has been actively
involved in maritime research and education in China.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.94.5" class="koboSpan">He has
been associated with numerous research projects and activities in the
field of maritime transport in China both at national and regional
levels. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.94.6"
class="koboSpan">He is the Director of two joint MSc programmes, which
he created in 2004, between WMU and two Chinese Maritime Universities in
Shanghai and Dalian.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.95.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Peter Marlow</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.96.1" class="koboSpan">Peter Marlow is
Professor of Maritime Economics and Logistics at Cardiff University in
the UK. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.96.2"
class="koboSpan">He has over 30 years’ experience in academia and
research work and is the author of more than 100 published works.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.96.3" class="koboSpan">He is
currently the Head of Logistics and Operations Management at the Cardiff
Business School and is a transport economist
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_page_xxii"></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.97.1"
class="koboSpan">with considerable expertise in maritime and land
transport as well as logistics.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.97.2" class="koboSpan">From
1998 to 2001 he was President of NEPTUNE, an EU-based network of
universities and research institutions and is currently President of the
International Association of Maritime Economists and Visiting Professor
at Dalian Maritime University.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.97.3" class="koboSpan">His
research interests include the fiscal treatment of shipping; the choice
of flag in international shipping; the value added by transport in
logistics supply chains; short sea shipping; port economics and
logistics; maritime clusters; and inter-modal transport.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.98.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Hilde Meersman</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.99.1" class="koboSpan">Hilde Meersman
has a PhD in Applied Economics.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.99.2" class="koboSpan">She is a
full professor at the University of Antwerp where she teaches in the
fields of Econometrics, Transport Modelling, and Economics.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.99.3" class="koboSpan">She also
teaches at the Technical University of Delft and has been guest
professor in a number of universities including MIT, Boston and IST,
Lisbon.</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.100.1" class="koboSpan">She is the
coordinator of the policy research centre of the Flemish Government:
‘Mobility and Public Works – Commodity Flows’ which is allocated at the
Department of Transport and Regional Economics of the University of
Antwerp.</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.101.1" class="koboSpan">She chaired
the International Scientific Committee of the WCTRS from 2001 until
2007. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.101.2"
class="koboSpan">She was able to build up a large experience in research
management and research coordination during her chairwomanship of the
Research Centre for Economic and Social Research of the University of
Antwerp.</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.102.1" class="koboSpan">Her research
activities are on the intersection of transportation economics,
macroeconomics and quantitative modelling.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.102.2" class="koboSpan">This
enables her to link the evolution in the world economy to specific
transportation problems.</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.103.1" class="koboSpan">She is
involved, directly or indirectly, in a large number of research projects
on topics such as international transport infrastructure investment,
modelling and forecasting transport, empirical analysis of port
competition, inland navigation, mode choice, sustainable mobility,
etc.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.104.1" class="koboSpan">Professor David Menachof</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.105.1" class="koboSpan">David Menachof
is the Peter Thompson Chair in Port Logistics, based at the Logistics
Institute at Hull University Business School.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.105.2" class="koboSpan">He
received his doctorate from the University of Tennessee, and was the
recipient of the Council of Logistics Management’s Doctoral Dissertation
Award in 1993. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.105.3"
class="koboSpan">He is a Fulbright Scholar, having spent an academic
year in Odessa, as an expert in Logistics and Distribution.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.105.4" class="koboSpan">He has
previously taught at the Cass Business School, City University London,
the University of Charleston, South Carolina, and the University of
Plymouth, England. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.105.5"
class="koboSpan">His research interests include supply chain security
and risk, global supply chain issues, liner shipping and
containerisation, and financial techniques applicable to
logistics.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.106.1" class="koboSpan">Dr Kyriaki Mitroussi</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.107.1" class="koboSpan">Kyriaki
Mitroussi was awarded her PhD in Management and Business at Cardiff
Business School, Cardiff University in 2001 as a scholar of the Greek
State Foundation of Scholarships.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.107.2" class="koboSpan">She
also holds an MSc in Marine Policy from Cardiff University, Department
of Maritime Studies and International Transport.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.107.3" class="koboSpan">She
joined Cardiff Business School as a lecturer in September 2005, and
prior to her current post she served as a lecturer at the University of
Piraeus, Department of Maritime Studies
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_page_xxiii"></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.108.1"
class="koboSpan">in undergraduate and postgraduate schemes.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.108.2" class="koboSpan">She has
worked with shipping companies and has also been involved in consultancy
services. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.108.3"
class="koboSpan">Her research work has been published in international
academic journals while articles have also appeared in the international
commercial and economic press.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.108.4" class="koboSpan">Her
broad research interests include: shipping management, third-party ship
management, safety and quality in shipping and shipping policy.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.108.5" class="koboSpan">She is
a member of the International Association of Maritime Economists.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.109.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Kunio Miyashita</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.110.1" class="koboSpan">Kunio
Miyashita is the Professor of International Logistics and Transportation
at the Faculty of Business Administration, Osaka Sangyo University,
Japan. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.110.2"
class="koboSpan">He is also the professor emeritus of Kobe University
and holds a PhD from this University.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.110.3" class="koboSpan">He is
the author of six books, including
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.111.1"
class="koboSpan">Market Behaviors in Competitive Shipping
Markets</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.112.1"
class="koboSpan">) and
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.113.1"
class="koboSpan">Global Competition of Japanese Logistics
Industry</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.114.1"
class="koboSpan">. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.114.2"
class="koboSpan">He is the President of the Japanese Society of
Transportation Economics, the former President of the Japanese Society
of Logistics and Shipping Economics, and the Honorary Editor-in-Chief of
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.115.1"
class="koboSpan">The Asian Journal of Shipping and
Logistics</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.116.1"
class="koboSpan">.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.117.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Enrico Musso</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.118.1" class="koboSpan">Enrico Musso
(Genoa 1962) is full professor in Applied Economics at the University of
Genoa, where he is involved in research and teaching activities in
Transport Economics, Maritime and Port Economics, and Urban and Regional
Planning. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.118.2"
class="koboSpan">Since 2008 he has been a member of the Italian
Senate.</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.119.1" class="koboSpan">Former
director of the PhD programme in
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.120.1"
class="koboSpan">Logistics, Infrastructure and
Territory</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.121.1"
class="koboSpan"> of the University of Genoa; lecturer in the Masters
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.122.1"
class="koboSpan">Transport and Maritime Management
</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.123.1"
class="koboSpan">and
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.124.1"
class="koboSpan">Transport and Maritime
Economics</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.125.1"
class="koboSpan">; visiting professor in many universities in Italy and
abroad; director of international research programmes concerning ports,
maritime transport, urban mobility.</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.126.1" class="koboSpan">Author,
co-author or editor of more than 130 scientific publications, among
which important volumes or chapters in volumes in maritime and port
economics.</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.127.1"
class="koboSpan">Editor-in-chief of the
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.128.1"
class="koboSpan">International Journal of Transport
Economics</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.129.1"
class="koboSpan">. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.129.2"
class="koboSpan">Member of the editorial board of
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.130.1"
class="koboSpan">Maritime Economics and
Logistics</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.131.1"
class="koboSpan"> and
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.132.1"
class="koboSpan">European
Transports</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.133.1"
class="koboSpan">.</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.134.1" class="koboSpan">Chairman of
the Italian Society of Transportation Economists.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.134.2"
class="koboSpan">Co-chair of the
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.135.1"
class="koboSpan">Maritime Transport and Ports Special Interest Group
</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.136.1"
class="koboSpan">at the
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.137.1"
class="koboSpan">World Conference on Transport Research
Society</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.138.1"
class="koboSpan">. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.138.2"
class="koboSpan">Co-founder of
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.139.1"
class="koboSpan">Transportnet</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.140.1"
class="koboSpan">, a research network of eight European universities,
and of the Italian Centre of Excellence for Integrated Logistics.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.141.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Nikos K. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.141.2" class="koboSpan">Nomikos</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.142.1" class="koboSpan">Nikos Nomikos
is a Professor in Shipping Risk Management and Director of the MSc
degree in Shipping, Trade and Finance at Cass Business School, City
University London. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.142.2"
class="koboSpan">He holds an MSc and PhD from Cass Business School.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.142.3" class="koboSpan">He
started his career at the Baltic exchange as Senior Market Analyst,
being in charge of the freight indices and risk management divisions.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.142.4" class="koboSpan">Since
November 2001, he has been with the Faculty of Finance at Cass Business
School where he specialises in the area of freight derivatives and risk
management. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.142.5"
class="koboSpan">His research papers on derivatives pricing and
modelling have been published in international journals and have been
presented
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_page_xxiv"></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.143.1"
class="koboSpan">in conferences worldwide.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.143.2" class="koboSpan">He has
also published a book on
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.144.1"
class="koboSpan">Shipping Derivatives and Risk
Management</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.145.1"
class="koboSpan"> and has developed postgraduate and executive
development courses in that area.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.146.1" class="koboSpan">Dr Lauri Ojala</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.147.1" class="koboSpan">Lauri Ojala is
Professor of Logistics at the Turku School of Economics, Finland.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.147.2" class="koboSpan">His
research interests include international logistics and transport
markets. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.147.3"
class="koboSpan">Since the mid-1990s, he has also worked as an expert
for several international agencies on development projects in for
example, the Baltic States, Albania, and several CIS states.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.147.4" class="koboSpan">From
2006 to 2008, he was in charge of two EU part-funded logistics projects
in the Baltic Sea Region.</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.148.1" class="koboSpan">He is
currently Project Director of another EU part-funded project on safety
and security of international road freight transport (CASH).</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.149.1" class="koboSpan">He is the
founder and co-author of the
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.150.1"
class="koboSpan">Logistics Performance
Index</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.151.1"
class="koboSpan"> first launched by The World Bank in November 2007.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.151.2" class="koboSpan">LPI
2010 was published in January.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.152.1" class="koboSpan">Dr Photis M. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.152.2" class="koboSpan">Panayides</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.153.1" class="koboSpan">Photis M.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.153.2"
class="koboSpan">Panayides is Associate Professor in Shipping Economics
at the Department of Commerce, Finance and Shipping, Cyprus University
of Technology. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.153.3"
class="koboSpan">He holds a first class Honours degree and a PhD in
Shipping Economics and Management (1998) from the University of
Plymouth, UK. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.153.4"
class="koboSpan">Photis held academic appointments among others at the
University of Plymouth, the Hong Kong Polytechnic University, the
Copenhagen Business School, and the National University of Singapore to
the level of Associate Professor.</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.154.1" class="koboSpan">Photis has
authored three books and over 30 scientific journal papers in the fields
of shipping economics, logistics and transportation.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.154.2" class="koboSpan">He
reviews for major journals and has contributed several conference
papers. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.154.3"
class="koboSpan">He pioneered the development of academic and
professional programmes in shipping and logistics and has also consulted
for several companies. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.154.4"
class="koboSpan">Photis is an elected member of the Board of the
International Association of Maritime Economists and serves on the Board
of Directors of the Cyprus Ports Authority.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.155.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Anastassios N. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.155.2" class="koboSpan">Perakis</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.156.1" class="koboSpan">A.N.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.156.2"
class="koboSpan">(Tassos) Perakis, a SNAME Fellow, obtained his Diploma
degree from NTU Athens (NA&ME), and his Masters (Ocean Eng/Operations
Research), PhD and MBA all from MIT.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.156.3" class="koboSpan">Tenured
faculty, Department of NA&ME, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.156.4"
class="koboSpan">Sponsored research: fleet deployment, logistics,
routing/scheduling, reliability/safety, environmental policy,
probabilistic modelling, optimisation, decision analysis for marine
systems. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.156.5"
class="koboSpan">Has authored one book, three chapters in edited books,
and over 150 refereed journal articles and conference proceedings,
reports, and other publications.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.156.6"
class="koboSpan">Visiting Professor, Technical University Berlin
(twice), NTU Athens (twice), Institute of Water Resources (USA), Boeing
Welliver Faculty Fellow (2003), Office of Naval Research Distinguished
Faculty Fellow (2003). </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.156.7"
class="koboSpan">Fellow, Michigan Memorial PhoenixEnergy Institute.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.156.8"
class="koboSpan">Numerous service activities, recently with US National
Acad. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.156.9"
class="koboSpan">of Sciences/Transportation Research Board panels.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.156.10"
class="koboSpan">Chaired seven graduated PhD students, three of them
also professors, several academic “grandchildren” and
“great-grandchildren”.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_page_xxv"></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.157.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Michael Roe</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.158.1" class="koboSpan">Michael Roe
holds the Chair of Maritime and Logistics Policy at the University of
Plymouth. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.158.2"
class="koboSpan">He previously worked with the Greater London Council
and the Universities of Aston, Coventry, London Metropolitan and City.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.158.3" class="koboSpan">The
author of over 50 refereed journal papers and 11 books, he specialises
in Eastern European maritime policy and the wider governance of maritime
affairs. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.158.4"
class="koboSpan">His wife, Liz, provides moral and intellectual support
whilst his children, Joe and Siân, provide entertainment and expenses.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.158.5" class="koboSpan">He has
active interests in modern European art and literature, restoring VW
Beetles, the work of Patti Smith and New Order and the exploits of
Charlton Athletic FC.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.159.1" class="koboSpan">Dr Merv Rowlinson</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.160.1" class="koboSpan">Merv Rowlinson
has served in towage and merchant shipping and has nearly 30 years’
teaching experience in shipping and logistics experience at the Merchant
Navy College, Warsash School of Navigation (Southampton) and London
Metropolitan University. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.160.2"
class="koboSpan">He has successfully supervised five PhD programmes.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.160.3" class="koboSpan">He has
an M.Phil from Liverpool Polytechnic and a PhD from the City of London
Polytechnic both in maritime business.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.160.4" class="koboSpan">He
currently divides his time between Copenhagen Business School, Hamburg
School of Shipping & Transportation, Lloyd’s Maritime Academy and the
European College of Business Management (London & Aachen).
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.160.5" class="koboSpan">His
research interests are inter-modal transport, particularly short sea
shipping and its potential for delivering sustainable transport.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.161.1" class="koboSpan">Dr William Sjostrom</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.162.1" class="koboSpan">William
Sjostrom is senior lecturer in economics at the Centre for Policy
Studies of the National University of Ireland, Cork, where he also
served as dean of the Faculty of Commerce and director of the Executive
MBA programme. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.162.2"
class="koboSpan">He previously taught economics at Northern Illinois
University and the University of Washington, was a staff economist at
the Port of Seattle, and has consulted for the Port of Cork, the
European Commission, and private law firms.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.162.3" class="koboSpan">He
serves on the editorial boards of
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.163.1"
class="koboSpan">Maritime Economics and
Logistics</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.164.1"
class="koboSpan"> and the
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.165.1"
class="koboSpan">International Journal of Transport
Economics</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.166.1"
class="koboSpan">. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.166.2"
class="koboSpan">His maritime research focuses primarily on competition
policy in liner shipping.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.166.3" class="koboSpan">He has
also published papers on crime, unemployment, competition law, and
oligopoly in the lumber industry.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.166.4" class="koboSpan">He
received his PhD in 1986 from the University of Washington, Seattle,
supervised by Keith Leffler, a specialist in the economics of
competition policy, and Douglas Fleming, a maritime geographer.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.167.1" class="koboSpan">Dr Martin Stopford</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.168.1" class="koboSpan">Martin
Stopford is a graduate of Oxford University and holds a PhD in
International Economics from London University.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.168.2" class="koboSpan">During
his 30-year career in the maritime industry he has held positions as
Director of Business Development with British Shipbuilders, Global
Shipping Economist with Chase Manhattan Bank NA, Chief Executive of
Lloyd’s Maritime Information Services and currently Managing Director of
Clarkson Research. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.168.3"
class="koboSpan">He is a Visiting Professor at Cass Business School,
City University London, and is a regular lecturer and course leader at
Cambridge Academy of Transport.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.168.4" class="koboSpan">His
publications include
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.169.1"
class="koboSpan">Maritime
Economics</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.170.1"
class="koboSpan">, the widely used shipping text, and many published
papers on shipping economics and ship finance.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_page_xxvi"></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.171.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Siri Pettersen Strandenes</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.172.1" class="koboSpan">Siri Pettersen
Strandenes is professor at the Department of Economics, Norwegian School
of Economics and Business Administration (NHH), and honorary visiting
professor in The Costas Grammenos International Centre for Shipping,
Trade and Finance at Cass Business School.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.172.2" class="koboSpan">Her
fields of research are transport and market analysis focusing on the
maritime and the airline industries.
</span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.172.3" class="koboSpan">She has
published in international research journals and is member of the
editorial board of the
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.173.1"
class="koboSpan">Maritime Economics &
Logistics</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.174.1"
class="koboSpan">. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.174.2"
class="koboSpan">She teaches graduate level courses in shipping and
international economics. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.174.3"
class="koboSpan">She is member of the board of DnB NOR ASA.</span>

## <span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.175.1" class="koboSpan">Professor Theodore C. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.175.2" class="koboSpan">Syriopoulos</span>

<span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.176.1" class="koboSpan">Theodore
Syriopoulos is Associate Professor of Finance in the Department of
Shipping, Trade and Transport, School of Business Studies, University of
the Aegean, Greece. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.176.2"
class="koboSpan">For more than fifteen years, he has served as a
Managing Director and Board Member in a number of private and public
companies in banking, investment, asset management and financial
consulting. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.176.3"
class="koboSpan">He researches and publishes regularly in international
academic journals, including the
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.177.1"
class="koboSpan">Journal of International Financial Markets,
Institutions & Money
</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.178.1"
class="koboSpan">and
</span><span class="italic"><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.179.1"
class="koboSpan">Applied Financial
Economics</span></span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.180.1"
class="koboSpan">. </span><span id="frontmatter3.xhtml_kobo.180.2"
class="koboSpan">Academic fields of interest include shipping finance,
capital markets and risk management, portfolio strategies, mergers &
acquisitions and corporate governance.
